_comment: Room / firmware PRESET metadata for the customer-friendly configuration mode (the file keeps its historical kits.json name to avoid compatibility churn — entries are INSTALLER PRESETS, never commercial availability declarations). Each entry maps deterministically to wizard state keys (mount, power, bathroom, airiq, ventiq, roomiq, fan, led, voice) and a firmware config_string that already exists in manifest.json. Do not add a preset without a matching config_string in manifest.json — the wizard will surface a 'no compatible firmware' error if the mapping is missing. This file is the DISPLAY layer only: it must never carry its own copy of a firmware version. The per-preset version shown in the picker is resolved live from the served manifest (config_string -> build.version, see scripts/app.js resolveKitVersions); the firmware_channel and the display_name below are pinned to the served source and to the canonical bundle names by the drift-guard in __tests__/kit-served-consistency.test.js so they can never silently drift from reality again (PRODUCT-KITS-CONSISTENCY-001). WEBFLASH-TAXONOMY-RECONCILE-001: presets are room/use-case led (room_label + recommended_rooms lead the customer experience; board names and the config string stay visible as technical detail). commercial_bundle_id joins each preset to its SOT bundle record in scripts/data/sot-commercial-mirror.json — SOT owns commercial names/status/buyability, and as mirrored today NO bundle is available or buyable, so no preset copy may ever say or imply on sale / buy now / commercially available. 'recommended' is an INSTALLER firmware recommendation only, never a commercial claim.
_authoring_notes: sku: stable, customer-facing kit identifier. Use the 'S360-KIT-...' prefix to keep these distinct from the per-module SKUs (S360-100, S360-200, ...) listed in CLAUDE.md.

wizard_state: state keys consumed by setState() in scripts/state.js. mount=ceiling is required (the wizard does not support wall mounts). power must be one of usb/poe/pwr. Module slots follow scripts/data/module-requirements.js.
firmware_config_string: must exactly match a build.config_string in manifest.json. The kit-config.js loader rejects entries that don't resolve.

firmware_channel: optional default channel preference. Provenance + release-channel UI still gate the actual install — kit metadata never bypasses those checks. The four preview room bundles resolve to preview manifest builds, so the engine's preview-channel acknowledgement applies at install time. Only the stable Bathroom PoE bundle installs without that acknowledgement.

WF2-KIT-BUNDLE-PICKER-001: restored the five customer room bundles deleted by the WebFlash 2.0 PR 13 cleanup. S360-KIT-BATH-P is the stable, default, recommended choice (Release-One Ceiling-POE-VentIQ-RoomIQ); the Kitchen/Bedroom/Living/Corridor bundles are preview-channel only and are never default, recommended, or buyable. Living and Corridor intentionally share the Ceiling-POE-RoomIQ-LED preview build as separate customer cards. The single legacy S360-KIT-CEILING-VENTIQ-ROOMIQ-POE entry was reconciled into S360-KIT-BATH-P rather than kept as a duplicate of the same stable build.

Standalone fan-only previews (Ceiling-POE-FanPWM, Ceiling-POE-FanDAC) and any FanTRIAC config are intentionally NOT room-bundle products and must never be added here — they stay reachable only through the advanced module builder. FanTRIAC stays build-blocked.

WF2-FAN-CONTROL-GATES-001: added the Bathroom Relay fan-control bundle (S360-KIT-BATH-P-REL → Ceiling-POE-VentIQ-FanRelay-RoomIQ, preview channel). It is a full room bundle (RoomIQ + VentIQ + relay fan), never recommended/stable/default/buyable. Selecting it requires the preview-channel acknowledgement (engine-owned, state.js) AND the additive fan-control acknowledgement layered in scripts/install.js; both must be confirmed before install. The FanDAC kit bundles (and their stronger analog address-switch acknowledgement) arrive later via WF-IMPORT-FAN-BUNDLES-001.

WF2-FAN-EXPANSION-001: surfaced the five full-composition fan bundles imported into the manifest by WF-IMPORT-FAN-BUNDLES-001 as preview kit cards (six to eleven kits). Two Bathroom fan variants (S360-KIT-BATH-P-PWM → Ceiling-POE-VentIQ-FanPWM-RoomIQ, S360-KIT-BATH-P-DAC → Ceiling-POE-VentIQ-FanDAC-RoomIQ) and three Kitchen fan variants (S360-KIT-KITCHEN-P-REL → Ceiling-POE-AirIQ-FanRelay-RoomIQ, S360-KIT-KITCHEN-P-PWM → Ceiling-POE-AirIQ-FanPWM-RoomIQ, S360-KIT-KITCHEN-P-DAC → Ceiling-POE-AirIQ-FanDAC-RoomIQ). All five are preview-channel full room bundles (RoomIQ + an air sensor + a fan driver), never recommended/stable/default/buyable. The acknowledgements are config-driven and apply automatically from WF2-FAN-CONTROL-GATES-001: all six fan kits require the fan-control acknowledgement, and the two FanDAC kits additionally require the analog fan address-switch acknowledgement, all layered in scripts/install.js on top of the engine-owned preview-channel gate. The two FanDAC kits combine FanDAC with VentIQ/AirIQ, which is exactly the analog address conflict the address-switch acknowledgement covers; the kit applies its config directly, so the advanced-builder AirIQ/DAC mutex never blocks the kit-card path. S360-KIT-BATH-P stays the only stable/recommended/default kit.

WF-H1-REIMPORT-CLEAN-001 (W1, decision R-D1): retired the five fan preview kit cards added by WF2-FAN-EXPANSION-001 (S360-KIT-BATH-P-PWM, S360-KIT-BATH-P-DAC, S360-KIT-KITCHEN-P-REL, S360-KIT-KITCHEN-P-PWM, S360-KIT-KITCHEN-P-DAC) because their v1.0.0-preview builds were built before the upstream credential gate (SEC-ESP-BUILD-GATES-001) and were delisted from firmware/sources.json — see the delisted_sources register there and docs/rebuild-clean-credentials-001.md. They stay out of kits.json until a post-gate rebuild of each config is imported under a fresh upstream eligibility decision. The stable Bathroom and Bedroom kits are untouched.

WF-CLEANUP-010 history: the 6 legacy sample kits (AirIQ-POE/USB/PWR, Core-USB, Fan-USB, Bathroom-VentIQ-POE) were removed because their firmware_config_string values were not published in manifest.json. LED is excluded from the STABLE Release-One config via firmware/sources.json block_tokens; LED room bundles here resolve only to the preview Ceiling-POE-RoomIQ-LED build.

PRODUCT-KITS-CONSISTENCY-001 (N1): fixed two display bugs the flasher screenshot exposed. (bug 2) Bedroom's description falsely read 'Preview firmware — acknowledge the preview channel before installing' while the config (Ceiling-POE-RoomIQ) is served stable v1.0.8 and its badge already keyed off the real stable channel; the description now matches reality. (bug 1) the per-kit version was never carried here — it is resolved live from the served manifest — so the fix was to LOCK that derivation with a contract test rather than re-author a number: __tests__/kit-served-consistency.test.js asserts every visible kit's firmware_channel and its served manifest version equal the reviewed served surface (__tests__/fixtures/expected-surface.json), that no visible kit maps to a non-release-ready (hardware-pending / compile-only / blocked) catalog config, and that each display_name matches the canonical consumer bundle name vendored in __tests__/fixtures/room-bundle-skus.json (mirrors config/room-bundle-skus.json in esphome-public). Display names were aligned to the 'Sense360 <Room> Bundle — PoE' canonical form. No firmware, sources.json served entry, manifest, or binary changed; the hardware-pending safety gate is preserved — no hardware-pending config was promoted or surfaced.

SENSE360-CANONICALISATION-001 PR 13: commercial identity now has exactly one source. The vendored __tests__/fixtures/room-bundle-skus.json naming fixture (a second, esphome-public-derived display-name authority) was retired; every visible preset's display_name is pinned to its SOT commercial bundle record (scripts/data/sot-commercial-mirror.json, joined by commercial_bundle_id) in BOTH __tests__/kit-served-consistency.test.js and __tests__/webflash-taxonomy-reconcile.test.js. SOT owns commercial names, status, visibility and buyability; the mirror is regenerated evidence, never authority; nothing here is or claims to be available or buyable.

kits.description: Presence, temperature, humidity and light sensing.
notes: Stable RoomIQ firmware. The Bathroom preset remains the installer's recommended default.
